items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I've known him practically all of my life.

ctx.x: for him. We didn't last too long, but in order to get back we went into Oklahoma City and we met, at that time, this same band that I was talking about, the Southern Serenaders.

Now the Southern Serenaders, at that time, they had in the band Hot Lips Page, who is from Corsicana, Texas, and later moved to Dallas. I've known him practically all of my life. Hot Lips Page at that time was playing like everything Louis Armstrong ever put out, note for note. If you put one in one room and one in another you could hardly tell them apart. What a great trumpet player!

They had another saxophone player, who I grew up with, named Bill Owens, and he was playing sax and clarinet, and Walter Page, was in the band. Jimmy Rushing was the singer. And by the way, Jimmy Rushing, the only thing saved us is Jimmy Rushing's people always owned a restaurant in Oklahoma City, and he made it possible for us to eat over there, and his parents' restaurant.
